messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — TidalWorks (tenant: tidalworks-prod) experiencing elevated error rate in VPC dedicated pool. 5xx rate 15% over last 3m, latency 2-3x baseline. Pager: @raj (oncall). Severity: P1.
raj: Oncall here. Acknowledging. Pulling logs and starting mitigation.
emma: Looking at the allocator and kv-cache metrics for their dedicated pool. I'm seeing steady connection timeouts to model shards + cache evictions. Could be network flapping between AZs in the customer's VPC or a resource degredation on the dedicated nodes.
kevin: Any immediate customer impact visible from console? per-route tokens show repeated retries and model responses truncated with 503. Lia/sales should we alert TidalWorks?
lia: Lia from product/CS — yes, please patch note to account team asap. I'll draft a short customer-facing blurb.
sophie: Ops — if we can isolate their tenant routing to a healthy subset of hosts, that should reduce cross-tenant noise. Suggest isolate routing + pin to a smaller safe model variant to reduce memory pressure.
raj: Plan: 1) isolate tenant routing to the primary healthy zone 2) pin TidalWorks to safe-compact model variant (less memory, conservative beam) 3) temporarily increase replicas on isolated pool if possible 4) monitor error/latency.
emma: Executing isolation + pin now. Commands:
```
# pin model for tenant to safe variant
rictl model pin --tenant tidalworks-prod --model tw-large --version safe-compact-v1
# route policy set to tenant-isolate (no cross-tenant binpacking)
rictl route set-policy --tenant tidalworks-prod --policy tenant-isolate --preferred-az us-west-2a
```
raj: Triggering replication scale-up: `rictl pool scale --pool tidalworks-dedicated --replicas 3`
deploy-bot: rollout started: model-pin tw-large@safe-compact-v1 for tenant tidalworks-prod. Changes will take ~45s to propagate.
emma: I ran a quick smoke test against the pinned variant: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"model":"tw-large","input":"hello"}'` — response latency ~420ms, 200 OK. Good sign.
kevin: Metrics starting to shift: 5xx rate down to 6% in 2m, median latency trending down. KV eviction rate halved on pinned nodes.
lia: I'm sending the customer note: "We've detected increased errors; we've isolated your traffic and temporarily routed to a safe model variant to stabilize performance. No action required on your side; we'll update you as we monitor."
raj: Monitoring for 15m. If stable, we'll keep isolation and pin for 4 hours while SRE continues root cause.
sophie: Quick checklist for RCA: collect network flow logs from their VPC, host-level memory and disk I/O for the dedicated nodes, and model shard ilog for last 3 hours. I'll start those exports now.
emma: Export commands queued. Also adding a temporary trace sampling for the tenant (30%) so we get richer traces for failed requests.
kevin: Noted a side-effect: some higher-cost requests (longer seq len) hit the compact variant's truncation ceiling. Lia, prepare a customer note: we may ask them to reduce max_tokens for a short window or we'll do a staged rollback to a slightly larger safe variant if they need longer responses.
lia: Drafting update including that tradeoff.
raj: After 20m of stability we can close pager and create a follow-up thread for postmortem. If errors creep above 8% we'll revert config and notify.
emma: 20m check-in: error rate steady at 3-4%, latency ~0.9x of pre-incident for typical requests. Pins remain.
deploy-bot: rollout completed: model-pin applied; route policy updated.
kevin: All exports in progress. Network traces show intermittent packet drops in us-west-2b between infra and the customer's VPC endpoint — filing infra ticket to cloud provider.
sophie: Filing infra ticket referencing our trace ids and affected hosts.
lia: Customer update sent and acknowledged: "thanks, appreciate the quick action."
raj: Closing pager in 1h unless we see regressions. Postmortem owners: Emma (SRE) & Lia (Customer) — target doc in 72h.
emma: Leaving notes: - mitigation: tenant isolation + model pin to safe-compact-v1 - reason: suspected inter-AZ network instability causing cache eviction and node instability - follow-ups: evaluate auto-pin policy triggers, add a circuit-breaker to detect repeated KV evictions and auto-isolate tenant.
raj: Thanks everyone. If anything spikes, re-open thread. :thumbsup:
